title: Cycle Flow: Reserve, Defer & Micro‑Tranche Framework for Capacity Allocation
creator: Sofia Ramos
description:
Problem: We regularly over- or under-commit engineering capacity during 6-week cycles, causing last-minute scope cuts or wasted sprint bandwidth. Existing playbooks focus on tranche sizing and surge lanes, but teams lack a lightweight operational pattern for continuous rebalancing inside a cycle.

Proposal: Introduce a ’Cycle Flow’ framework that combines: (1) a small, explicitly reserved capacity buffer (Reserve Lanes) per cross-functional program; (2) a deferred-scope queue with clear deprecation criteria; and (3) micro-tranches for rapid swap-in/out of work. The framework includes a quantitative scoring model to prioritize deferrable work by customer impact, compliance risk, and unblock cost, plus a substitution matrix that identifies cross-team people-level swaps.

Goals: Reduce mid-cycle scope cuts that impact OKRs by 40% and reduce unplanned overtime during the last two weeks of a cycle by 30% vs. previous three cycles. Make scope deferral decisions data-driven and auditable in the console of record for cycle planning.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented Reserve Lane policy (percent of capacity per program) approved by GTM/Product/Eng. 2) Deferral scoring rubric published and applied to all candidate cut items in the cycle planning doc. 3) Two pilot squads run the micro-tranche swap process during Cycle 2026-W11 with metrics captured (swap latency, reopened work rate). 4) Dashboard shows reserve utilization and carryover rate; alerts for >50% unplanned consumption. 5) Post-cycle retrospective captures decisions and updates the rubric.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Sofia Ramos: Kickoff with PMs and Eng Leads. Shared initial rubric draft in CycleOps Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CYCLE/Reserve+and+Defer+Framework). Asked Eng to provide historical carryover rates by squad for last 6 cycles.

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Eng leads supplied burn-rate CSV (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-burn-rates). Early analysis: two teams consistently exceed planned velocity due to unplanned infra work; suggests we should carve an 'infra contingency' out of reserve lanes.

2026-03-02 - Design review (Amy Chen): Proposed micro-tranche ticket template and lifecycle. Design suggested adding a lightweight tag 'defer-candidate' and an owner field to avoid orphaned items. Added template to docs (Drive link shared in thread).

2026-03-04 - Engineering feedback (Priya Patel): Raised concern about cross-team substitution feasibility during high hiring freezes. Suggested adding a 'skill-similarity' score to the substitution matrix to avoid unrealistic swaps.

2026-03-07 - PM review (Carlos Vega): Updated scoring weights to emphasize customer-impact for revenue-facing products and compliance risk for Private/B2B integrations. Approved pilot with two squads: 'Embeddings' and 'Dedicated-UX'.

2026-03-09 - Liam O'Connor: Drafted Jira/Linear workflow changes and created automation spec for reserve lane consumption events (alerts to program lead when reserve dips below 40%). Created initial PR for automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycleops/pull/378

2026-03-10 - Sofia Ramos: Executive sync. High-level rollup spreadsheet and success metrics sent to GTM and Eng. Q&A: requested tighter definition for 'carryover' vs 'deferred' for metrics consistency. Action: finalize definitions by 2026-03-12.
